newsitem.title: USA: Rexrodt - trade, economy issues at centre of G7 talks.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt - trade, economy issues at centre of G7 talks.

text.p: Trade and economic issues are at the center of the Group of Seven industrialized nations' talks in Denver, with better trade plans also seen as the way forward to help developing countries, Germany's Guenter Rexrodt said.

Rexrodt, who is Germany's economics minister, told a breakfast briefing during the G7 summit meeting in Denver, Colorado: "Economic and trade issues are at the center of the conference. The problems in Africa, for example, also have a strong link to these issues."

Turning to the overall economic situation, Rexrodt said the G7 countries were in favor of maintaining inflation-free growth in the long term, making use of increased globalization to give new vigor to the world economy.
"The current position is that globalisation is being seen by all as the driving force for more growth. That means enormous opportunities," he said.
"What we want is sustainable inflation-free growth accompanied by stability policies and structural reform where it is needed...as well as open markets," Rexrodt said.
